subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Where are non-metals generally found in the periodic table?
questions.explain: Non-metals are located on the right-hand side of the periodic table.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: Protons carry a relative charge of +1.

questions.q: Which element is in Group 7 and Period 3 of the periodic table?
questions.explain: Chlorine is in Group 7 (halogens) and Period 3.

questions.q: The halogens exist as molecules made of:
questions.explain: Halogens are diatomic, e.g. Cl2, Br2 and I2.

questions.q: Chlorine has two isotopes: 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
Which displacement reaction will happen?
options: Iodine displaces chlorine from sodium chloride
Bromine displaces chlorine from sodium chloride
Chlorine displaces bromine from sodium bromide
Chlorine displaces fluorine from sodium fluoride
questions.explain: A more reactive halogen (chlorine) displaces a less reactive one (bromine) from its salt.

questions.q: Going across a period from left to right, elements change from:
questions.explain: Across a period elements change from metals on the left to non-metals on the right.

questions.q: Compared with Group 1 metals, transition metals are generally:
questions.explain: Transition metals are typically harder, stronger, denser and less reactive than Group 1 metals.

questions.q: Which halogen is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Fluorine, at the top of Group 7, is the most reactive halogen.

questions.q: Which statement about a mixture is correct?
options: It can only be separated by chemical reactions
It always has a fixed composition
Its substances are not chemically combined and keep their properties
Its substances are chemically bonded together
questions.explain: In a mixture the substances are not chemically joined, so they can be separated by physical means.

questions.q: What is produced when a Group 1 metal reacts with water?
questions.explain: Group 1 metals react with water to form a metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Lithium reacts with water. Which observation is correct?
options: It fizzes and floats, releasing hydrogen
questions.explain: Lithium floats and fizzes on water, giving off hydrogen and forming lithium hydroxide.

questions.q: Why are the Group 0 noble gases unreactive?
options: They have a full outer shell of electrons
questions.explain: Noble gases have full (stable) outer electron shells, so they rarely react.

questions.q: How does the reactivity of the Group 1 alkali metals change going down the group?
questions.explain: Reactivity increases down Group 1 as the outer electron is more easily lost.

questions.q: An atom of fluorine has a mass number of 19 and atomic number of 9. How many neutrons does it have?
questions.explain: Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number = 19 - 9 = 10.

questions.q: What colour and state is bromine at room temperature?
questions.explain: Bromine is an orange-brown (red-brown) liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: What is the electronic structure of magnesium (12 electrons)?
questions.explain: Filling 2 then 8 then 2 gives 2,8,2 for 12 electrons.

questions.q: Why is the relative mass of an electron taken as very small?
options: An electron's mass is negligible compared with a proton or neutron
questions.explain: An electron's mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, so it is treated as negligible.

questions.q: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of:
questions.explain: Group number matches the number of electrons in the outer shell.

questions.q: Which property is typical of transition metals but not Group 1 metals?
options: They are solids at room temperature
questions.explain: Transition metals commonly form coloured compounds and act as catalysts.

questions.q: How many electrons can the first (innermost) shell of an atom hold?
questions.explain: The first shell holds a maximum of 2 electrons.

questions.q: Which of these is a property typical of Group 1 metals?
questions.explain: Alkali metals are soft enough to cut with a knife and have low densities.
